title: Language Model Extraction with Deterministic Reconciliation of Financial Statements
abstract: Language models are increasingly used to read unstructured financial documents, yet their outputs are probabilistic and difficult to audit. This study separates the two tasks involved in reconciliation. A language model extracts transactions from mobile money, bank and sales representative statements into a validated schema, and a deterministic rule decides whether each transaction matches an invoice. The study measures whether extraction under this arrangement is accurate enough for reconciliation, and at what cost and latency.

sections.heading: Motivation
body: Distributors reconcile payments received through several channels against the invoices they have issued. The statements arrive in inconsistent formats, and manual reconciliation is slow and prone to error. A language model can read these formats, but a reconciliation decision made by a model cannot be explained or reproduced with the certainty that financial records require.

sections.heading: Research question
body: Whether a language model can extract transactions from mobile money, bank and sales representative statements with sufficient accuracy for reconciliation, when every matching decision is reserved for a deterministic rule.

sections.heading: Method
body: A labelled evaluation set of statements is prepared, with the expected transactions recorded for each. Each model version extracts transactions into a schema, and records that fail validation are routed to manual review rather than reconciled. A deterministic matcher then pairs the extracted transactions with invoices. Results are compared across model versions with all other conditions held constant.

sections.heading: Measures
list: Field-level extraction accuracy for amount, date, reference and counterparty.
Reconciliation match rate against the labelled expectation.
Proportion of records routed to manual review.
Cost per statement and p95 latency for each model version.

sections.heading: Deliverables
body: A specification of the matching rule, an evaluation report and a reference implementation.

question: Whether a language model can extract transactions from mobile money, bank and sales representative statements with sufficient accuracy for reconciliation, when every matching decision is reserved for a deterministic rule.
method: A labelled evaluation set measures field-level extraction accuracy and the reconciliation match rate across model versions, together with cost per statement and p95 latency.
deliverables: A specification of the matching rule, an evaluation report and a reference implementation.
